title: Self-referential PackedScene should clearly hint at user error
body: ### Tested versions Godot_v4.5.1-stable_linux.x86_64 ### System information Ubuntu ### Issue description I have a slime in my game that clones itself. I'll reuse this clone skill for some other enemies as well, so I implemented this by exporting a `cloneScene` property on my slime and implementing a method that does the instantiating. When I assign the `cloneScene` to `slime.tscn` it shows in the Editor as assigned, but crashes at runtime because the value is null. (It probably did perform the assignment for the scene loaded in the editor, but then can't bootstrap the slime when it loads the game) **Expected Behavior** The instantiation is circular, hence the issue. This makes sense. However, the UX is confusing, because the editor is happy to assign the property. In the attached MRP it's evident the scene structure is circular, but in my real project this was tricky to see because multiple node layers of `Stat`s and `Skill`s were involved between the slime and the clone skill. * ~~I suggest we display a clear error message as soon as a circular/self-referential PackedScene is assigned to an exported variable.~~ * Ah, there **is** an error message. It's shown in the Output tab when I save slime.tscn. However, this is an unfortunate spot for it, because I often don't save. I launch the game with F5 which saves on its own 😉 . And when you do that, this error message vanishes and isn't shown again until you resave the slime.tscn for some other reason (even then, you'd have to catch it before you launch the game the next time). I swear I'm not trying to be pedantic here; I didn't even notice the error message until I started opening older Godot versions for regression testing, because at this time I was _searching_ for an error message. * I suggest the value should reset to null **immediately** to communicate to the user that the assignment is invalid. It currently only resets to null when reopening the project (without error message!). Or maybe there is a way we can at least emit an error message at runtime, when the slime PackedScene tries to load initially and detects a cycle? ### Steps to reproduce Open the MRP, assign the slime itself to the Slime's `cloneScene` property, launch the game. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [packed-scene-clone-is-null-mrp_2025-12-13_09-34-31.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24140710/packed-scene-clone-is-null-mrp_2025-12-13_09-34-31.zip)
